at.description: ISO-8601 BF event-occurrence time (same value as the BF journal entry `at`).

code.description: Machine-readable rejection code. Instrument-resolution codes: `instrument_unresolvable` (no broker symbol in the binding or target.instrument.broker_symbol, or the broker does not know it), `instrument_mismatch` (the broker asset behind broker_symbol disagrees with the deal's exchange/board/ticker), `instrument_delisted` (the instrument was delisted/archived at the broker), `unsupported` (the BF/connector cannot execute this deal, e.g. an unsupported mode/market).

command_type.description: Command type of the AFB command that was rejected. Absent for rejections not caused by an AFB command (e.g. execution: the broker rejected the entry order).

brokerError.description: Structured broker error behind the rejection. BF sends it only for USER-kind errors (those that must reach the user). Dictionary of `kind` is part of the contract: the frontend picks the user text by it. DAEMON-kind errors (unavailable, timeout, rate_limited, session_closed, trading_halted, auction_only, auth_expired) are handled by the BF daemon itself, never become a rejection and are never sent here. `native_code`/`native_message` are exactly as the broker returned them, unprocessed.

kind.description: BF error dictionary (USER kinds): `insufficient_funds`, `invalid_order`, `instrument_not_found`, `instrument_not_tradable`, `permission_denied`, `auth_failed`, `rejected` (broker refused for an unknown reason), `unknown`. The set may grow: a consumer MUST tolerate an unknown value (show native_message, fall back to `code`/`message`).

native_code.description: Broker's own error code as a string (e.g. `145`), null if the broker gave none.

native_message.description: Broker's own error text, unprocessed; null if none.
